problem.summary: Installing numpy 1.24 on Python 3.12 fails while building from source because the build backend imports distutils, which was removed from the standard library in Python 3.12.
problem.raw_logs:
Collecting numpy==1.24.4
  Getting requirements to build wheel ... error
  ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'distutils'

failed_approaches.why_it_failed: The isolated build environment does not see the upgraded setuptools, and numpy 1.24 has no cp312 wheel.
The package does not exist for Python 3.12 on Ubuntu 24.04.

solution.root_cause: numpy < 1.26 ships no wheels for CPython 3.12, so pip falls back to a source build whose build system depends on distutils, removed in Python 3.12 (PEP 632).
steps: Check which numpy versions publish cp312 wheels: 1.26.0 is the first.
Relax the pin in requirements.txt from numpy==1.24.4 to numpy>=1.26,<2.
Reinstall and run the test suite to confirm API compatibility.

shell_commands_executed.purpose: Reinstall dependencies with the updated pin.

verification_method.description: Full test suite passes after reinstalling.

problem.error_message: RuntimeError: CUDA error: no kernel image is available for execution on the device
problem.summary: PyTorch fails on the first CUDA kernel launch on an RTX 5090 (Blackwell, sm_120) even though torch.cuda.is_available() returns True.
problem.raw_logs:
UserWarning: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 with CUDA capability sm_120 is not compatible with the current PyTorch installation.
The current PyTorch install supports CUDA capabilities sm_50 sm_60 sm_70 sm_75 sm_80 sm_86 sm_90.
RuntimeError: CUDA error: no kernel image is available for execution on the device

failed_approaches.why_it_failed: The driver already supports sm_120. The torch wheel itself has no sm_120 kernels.
That variable only affects source builds and extensions, not prebuilt wheels.

solution.root_cause: Wheels built against CUDA 12.4 do not contain kernels for compute capability 12.0. Blackwell GPUs need PyTorch 2.7 or newer built against CUDA 12.8.
steps: Confirm the GPU capability with torch.cuda.get_device_capability() (returns (12, 0)).
Uninstall the cu124 build and install a cu128 build from the PyTorch index.
Run a small matmul on the GPU to verify kernels load.

shell_commands_executed.command: pip install torch torchvision torchaudio --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128
shell_commands_executed.purpose: Install a build with sm_120 kernels.

verification_method.description: A GPU matmul runs without errors.

problem.summary: uv was installed with the official installer inside a Docker build step, but the next RUN step cannot find it because the install directory is not on PATH in non-login shells.
problem.raw_logs:
#7 [4/6] RUN uv sync --frozen
#7 0.112 /bin/sh: 1: uv: not found
#7 ERROR: process "/bin/sh -c uv sync --frozen" did not complete successfully: exit code: 127

failed_approaches.approach: source ~/.bashrc in the next RUN step
failed_approaches.why_it_failed: RUN uses /bin/sh, which does not read .bashrc.

solution.root_cause: The installer places uv in $HOME/.local/bin and only updates shell profiles. Each Dockerfile RUN starts a fresh non-login /bin/sh that never reads them.
steps: Prefer copying the uv binary from the official image instead of running the installer.
If the installer is required, add $HOME/.local/bin to PATH with ENV so every later step sees it.

shell_commands_executed.purpose: Install uv with the official installer.

code_patches.description: Copy uv from its image instead of piping an installer.
code_patches.diff:
--- a/Dockerfile
+++ b/Dockerfile
@@ -3,4 +3,4 @@
 FROM python:3.13-slim
-RUN curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
+COPY --from=ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.8.4 /uv /uvx /bin/
 WORKDIR /app
 RUN uv sync --frozen

verification_method.description: docker build completes and uv sync runs.

problem.summary: npm start of a Create React App 4 project crashes on Node 17+ with error 0308010C (ERR_OSSL_EVP_UNSUPPORTED) during webpack compilation.
problem.raw_logs:
Error: error:0308010C:digital envelope routines::unsupported
    at new Hash (node:internal/crypto/hash:69:19)
    at Object.createHash (node:crypto:133:10)
    at module.exports (node_modules/webpack/lib/util/createHash.js:135:53)
  opensslErrorStack: [ 'error:03000086:digital envelope routines::initialization error' ],
  code: 'ERR_OSSL_EVP_UNSUPPORTED'

failed_approaches.why_it_failed: The dependency tree is identical; webpack 4 still requests MD4.

solution.root_cause: Node 17+ ships OpenSSL 3, which disables the MD4 hash by default. webpack 4 uses MD4 for module hashing.
steps: Upgrade to react-scripts 5, which uses webpack 5 and does not need MD4.
Only if upgrading is impossible, start with NODE_OPTIONS=--openssl-legacy-provider as a temporary workaround.

shell_commands_executed.purpose: Fallback for projects that cannot upgrade yet.

problem.error_message: fatal: detected dubious ownership in repository at '/__w/app/app'
problem.summary: Every git command fails inside a CI job container because the checked-out repository is owned by a different user than the one running git.
problem.raw_logs:
fatal: detected dubious ownership in repository at '/__w/app/app'
To add an exception for this directory, call:

	git config --global --add safe.directory /__w/app/app
Error: Process completed with exit code 128.

failed_approaches.approach: chown -R the workspace in a previous step
failed_approaches.why_it_failed: The runner recreates the mount with its own owner for each job container step.

solution.root_cause: Since git 2.35.2, git refuses to operate on repositories owned by another user (CVE-2022-24765). CI runners mount the workspace with the host user's UID while the container runs as root.
steps: Add only the workspace directory to safe.directory before any git command.
Avoid safe.directory '*', which disables the protection everywhere.

shell_commands_executed.purpose: Broader alternative tried first; not recommended.

verification_method.description: git status succeeds in the job.

problem.summary: A crew with 12 parallel agents hits 429 rate_limit_error bursts; the built-in retries all fire at the same moment and fail again.
problem.raw_logs:
anthropic.RateLimitError: Error code: 429 - {'type': 'error', 'error': {'type': 'rate_limit_error', 'message': 'Number of request tokens has exceeded your per-minute rate limit'}}
retry-after: 18

failed_approaches.why_it_failed: All agents retried on the same schedule and collided again (thundering herd).

solution.root_cause: Concurrent agents share one per-minute token budget. Synchronised retries without jitter and without honouring retry-after reproduce the burst.
steps: Cap concurrency with a shared semaphore sized to the token budget.
Honour the retry-after header and add full jitter to the backoff.

code_patches.diff:
--- a/app/llm.py
+++ b/app/llm.py
@@ -1,6 +1,14 @@
+import asyncio, random
+_slots = asyncio.Semaphore(4)
+
 async def complete(client, **kw):
-    return await client.messages.create(**kw)
+    for attempt in range(6):
+        async with _slots:
+            try:
+                return await client.messages.create(**kw)
+            except RateLimitError as e:
+                wait = float(e.response.headers.get("retry-after", 2 ** attempt))
+        await asyncio.sleep(wait + random.uniform(0, wait))
+    raise RuntimeError("rate limited after 6 attempts")

verification_method.description: The 12-agent crew completes with zero failed calls.

problem.summary: An image built on an Apple Silicon Mac starts fine locally but crashes immediately on the x86_64 production cluster with exec format error.
problem.raw_logs:
kubectl logs api-7c9f8d-x2lq
exec /usr/local/bin/docker-entrypoint.sh: exec format error
Back-off restarting failed container

failed_approaches.why_it_failed: Permissions were correct; the binaries in the image are arm64.

solution.root_cause: docker build on Apple Silicon produces linux/arm64 images by default. The x86_64 nodes cannot execute arm64 binaries.
steps: Build for the target platform explicitly with buildx.
Publish a multi-arch manifest so both laptops and servers pull a native image.

shell_commands_executed.purpose: Build and push a multi-arch image.

verification_method.description: The manifest lists both platforms and the pod reaches Running.

problem.error_message: Error: Hydration failed because the server rendered text didn't match the client.
problem.summary: A Next.js 15 page shows a hydration error on every load because a timestamp is formatted with toLocaleString() in a component rendered on both server and client.
problem.raw_logs:
Error: Hydration failed because the server rendered text didn't match the client.
+ 14/03/2026, 09:12:44
- 3/14/2026, 9:12:44 AM

failed_approaches.approach: Add suppressHydrationWarning to the parent div
failed_approaches.why_it_failed: It only applies one level deep and hides a real mismatch.

solution.root_cause: The server and the browser use different locales and time zones, so the formatted string differs between the two renders.
steps: Format dates with an explicit locale and timeZone so both renders agree.
Or render the time only on the client after mount.

verification_method.description: No hydration warning in the browser console after reload.

problem.error_message: psycopg2.OperationalError: SCRAM authentication requires libpq version 10 or above
problem.summary: Connecting to PostgreSQL 16 from an old host fails because psycopg2 is linked against the system libpq 9.2, which cannot do scram-sha-256 authentication.
problem.raw_logs: psycopg2.OperationalError: SCRAM authentication requires libpq version 10 or above

failed_approaches.approach: Switch the server to md5 auth
failed_approaches.why_it_failed: Not allowed by the managed database policy, and weaker.

solution.root_cause: psycopg2 built from source links the system libpq. Amazon Linux 2 ships libpq 9.2, which predates SCRAM support.
steps: Install a newer libpq, or use psycopg2-binary which bundles a recent one.
Verify with psycopg2.__libpq_version__ >= 100000.

shell_commands_executed.purpose: Install a libpq with SCRAM support.
Use the wheel that bundles libpq 16.

verification_method.description: libpq version check and a connection succeed.
